svg.title: TOPAK D3 — The record planes: what is ordered, what is carried, what is kept, what is erased
svg.desc: Four stores hold the record. The Paxos log orders; Kafka carries; the archive is the system of record; a separately governed store holds plaintext so it can be destroyed. Across all four runs the plane boundary (B5): control-plane facts cross and survive, cognitive payloads are reduced to a hash and a pointer.
svg.text: TOPAK · D3

text.tspan: The record planes: what is ordered, what is carried, what is kept, what is erased

svg.text: Four stores hold the record. The Paxos log orders; Kafka carries; the archive is the system of record; a separately governed store holds plaintext so it can be destroyed. Across all four runs the plane boundary (B5): control-plane facts cross and survive, cognitive payloads are reduced to a hash and a pointer.
The ordering authority and the causal frame (ADR-0015; ADR-0005). Every effect has a
consensus-ordered, signed, authorizing predecessor here; the log index is the fence. Neither the
topic nor the emission is the record; the log is (ToO §4.4). No snapshots or compaction at the
reference (G14).
Every Entry: Grant, Renew, Admit, EndRound, Revoke, EpochIncrement, Issue, GatesPassed,
BreakGlassApprove.
Admits are F1; a vote's admit is F3; stops are F2; issuances F4; break-glass admits F5; erasure
events would be F6 (unbuilt).
Denials are not here: a denial changes no state, so it is never proposed.
None. A payload appears only as a digest: Draft content, Emit/Report records, Invoke/
Actuate inputs, the frozen input (Admitted, state.rs).
Transport with a durability window (acks=all), neither ordering authority nor system of record.
One single-partition topic per principal per epoch or round, sealed, per-topic ACL, per-use retention,
the unit of erasure (ADR-0003). The reference's K row is carried as a debt against ADR-0005, still
Proposed (ADR-0033 §2).
Every record's envelope: kind, seat, fence, the authorizing admit index, the per-lease sequence
number, the payload digest (headers topak-*).
Denial records (no admit, no sequence) while the round is open; the Actuate record of
ADR-0042 §3; heartbeats; the seal marker.
Written only after the admit commits; denials unordered, by the deciding replica.
Emit and Report bodies; an Actuate record's inputs and result themselves, under the topic's
ACL and in the round's unit of erasure (ADR-0042 §3).
A vote's emission carries the vote and a hash-and-pointer to its commentary, not the
commentary (ToO §4.4).
Cognitive intermediate state (scratchpads, chains of thought) is never written to round topics
The system of record (ADR-0005, Proposed; ADR-0004, Accepted, is scoped to it). Fed by its
own ETL per use case; not a tier of the topic: read under its own authority, it neither extends a
topic's life nor survives its erasure (ADR-0003 A3). The reference writes archive.jsonl per
replica, a projection of the log, which is not this archive (G9).
The control-plane record keeps a hash and a pointer for every cognitive payload (ADR-0004).
Trace conformance needs actions, identities and ordering, not prompt text: the archive holds what
replay and conformance need (ADR-0004 Context).
Six forensic classes are non-erasable here for the declared horizon (ADR-0028).
None in plaintext: a hash and a pointer per payload.
Plaintext lives in a store built for deletion (ADR-0004). Its readers are where the replay-harness
attestation requirement attaches; the pointer to it is itself a disclosure (demand type 5, declined).
None: the store holds payloads only.
Its entries are reached by the archive's pointers, and erased by deleting them (ADR-0006).
Prompts, reasoning, review commentary: all erasable. No cognitive payload is in the forensic
floor (ADR-0028 §1).
B5 plane boundary · facts cross and survive; payloads are reduced to hash + pointer

svg.text: Identity: topak.<chain>.<domain>.<seat>.e<epoch>.r<round>. The rules-epoch chain is part of the name (ADR-0003 A1): re-genesis restarts epochs and rounds at zero, and two development resets once wrote into the same Kafka topic (finding 4). A sealed topic is never written again.

text.tspan: ADR-0003, clause by clause (clause annotation C1, with A1–A3)

svg.text: Topic per principal per epoch/round
No
Core; 0003.2 and 0003.3 have no meaning without it
A topic is identified by its rules-epoch chain as well as by principal and epoch/round
Ratified 2026.09.25 (Batch 5); not confirmation-required. Finding 4
Sealed on emit completion
No
Core; defines the unit of erasure
One companion topic, after, for denials after the seal: never an emission, same ACL and retention, dropped
with the round; bounded, with a marker
Ratified 2026.09.25 (Batch 5); confirmation-required C1. Finding 11
Per-topic ACL model
No
Follows from 0003.1
Retention scoping
Entangled with the open raw-emission retention question (0003 vs 0006). Likely first to be superseded
Replay authorization
Overlaps ADR-0020: authorization to replay and the scope of replay are different decisions
Wrapper-Rego masking
Confirmed independently supersedable. Not built at the reference
No tiered storage
Operational; a degeneracy candidate under ADR-0023
No tiered storage is one store for a topic's whole retention, not a retention length; the archive is not a tier
Ratified 2026.09.30 (Batch 17) as a scoping, not a reversal
Separate read-only principals for audit; archive is its own ETL per use case
Carry no clause number (S3-2)
The authoritative vote is the admit decision in the log, which F3 retains.
The voter's round-topic emission carries the vote together with a hash-and-pointer to its commentary in the separately governed store; the commentary is what erasure removes.
Without the split the record contradicts itself: a topic holding vote and commentary is either erasable as a unit, losing F3, or unerasable, losing the commentary's erasability.
A Build round is one pipeline invocation; each seat holds its own topic, sealed when the artifact is submitted to the gate (§3).
Every vote covers artifact digest ∧ sealed topic-set digest (§4): voters sign provenance, not only the product.
Retained for the production lifetime of any artifact promoted from the round (§7); the topic stays the unit of erasure.

text.tspan: Replay reconstructs what crossed the membrane (ADR-0020)

svg.text: The replayable record of a round: actions attempted, including those denied; effects emitted; lease and epoch transitions; the Persona binding in force.
The Observer and replay read the same stream: no privileged channel, so detection latency L stays an honest number.
Root-cause analysis can establish what a principal did, never why.

text.tspan: Ordering across topics comes from the log (ToO §4.2)

svg.text: Within-partition order gives no global timeline once there is a topic per round. An emission carries the admit's log index, the fence and a per-lease sequence number, which covers ADR-0015's one residual:
effects admitted in a round and emitted at different times (G15).
It leaves a verifying envelope over unreadable ciphertext, a hole no auditor can tell from suppression (ADR-0003 Context; ToO §4.3).
Erasure is deletion of sealed topics and of plaintext-store entries (ADR-0006).
Topic count scales with principals × rounds: broker metadata pressure needs a lifecycle story.
A masking miss has a blast radius of one round. Re-genesis migration of read access is open (G17).
